heading: INT. NEONATAL ICU, NIGHT SHIFT - 4 A.M.

units.text: INT. NEONATAL ICU, NIGHT SHIFT - 4 A.M.
Rows of incubators glow like small amber lanterns.
Monitors blink green.
A radiator ticks.
No one is at the nurses' station.
The desk phone's red light flashes.
An answering machine clicks on.
You've reached Neonatal. If this is an emergency, hang up and call the floor line. Otherwise, leave your message after the tone.
units.name: PHILOMENA

units.text: Beep.
Dead air.
Then a click, and the line goes silent.
The double doors swing open.
DR. PHILOMENA ADEGBOYE-LINDGREN (40s, scrubs, hair under a cap, a coffee cup in each hand) pushes through backward, shouldering the door.
She sets one coffee on the desk, takes a sip of the other, and looks at the flashing phone.
She presses the button.
The message plays again.
She listens to the beep, the silence, the click.
She frowns.
She picks up the receiver, checks the dial tone, replaces it.
She walks the row of incubators.
At each one she checks the monitor, taps the chart, nods.
At the fourth she stops, reaching to adjust a blanket.
Her hand hovers.
The baby is awake.
Eyes open.
Staring at her without blinking.
She smiles, adjusts the blanket, and moves on.
At the sixth incubator she stops again.
Empty.
A name card still clipped to the frame.
She checks the chart.
Her pen stops.
Where did you go?
units.name: PHILOMENA

units.text: She looks back toward the desk.
The red light has stopped flashing.
She walks slowly toward it.
Beside the phone lies a hospital bracelet, tiny, the plastic still warm.
She picks it up.
Turns it over.
On the back, in fresh marker: HER NAME.
The monitors all flatline at once.
No.
units.name: PHILOMENA

units.text: She spins.
The row of incubators stands in perfect order.
Every one of them is empty.
Every one of them is lit.
The answering machine clicks on again.
You've reached Neonatal. Leave your message after the tone.
units.name: PHILOMENA

units.text: Beep.
And this time, a small breath on the line.
